documentation.title: Large sliding: a pairing that GROWS still has somewhere to assemble
documentation.description:
Regression gate for the matrix-graph reservation, on the one configuration that used to abort: a FORCE-CARRYING pair whose set of (secondary element, primary element) blocks GROWS while the body slides.
The mesh and the slide are ContactSlidingMortar2d's -- the four-face tent, one secondary LINE3 dragged 0.7 in x -- with applyContactForce="yes". Sliding takes the secondary element from straddling two primary faces to straddling three, so the assembler element list goes 2 -> 3.
WHAT USED TO HAPPEN. The sparsity pattern is built once, from the element list as it stands before the first solve, so the third block had no reserved entries and the run died inside CRS_Matrix with an index-pair-not-found error that names nothing about contact. Note that this happened even though NO point is in contact here: an element with no active point still assembles a correctly shaped zero block, and a zero still has to be added somewhere.
WHAT HAPPENS NOW. ReserveGraphPrimaries() records, once and on the reference configuration, every primary element each secondary element could plausibly reach, and BuildElementList() emits an assembler element for all of them -- empty where nothing projects there. The list is then independent of the current pairing, so the graph still covers the pairing after the body has slid.
numContactElements 2 -> 3 the pairing grows; this is the whole point numCells 2 -> 3 and the partition is re-cut with it numPoints 4 -> 6 numReservedElements 2 the reservation is live numActivePoints 0 nothing touches, and nothing has to
NOTHING TOUCHES, deliberately: the abort this locks out happened with an empty active set, because zero blocks are assembled like any other, and keeping it empty means the assertion cannot be disturbed by an elasticity solution. This is therefore not a force-carrying large-sliding BENCHMARK; no load flows across the interface.
